points.text: States the proton number gives 12 protons and, for a neutral atom, 12 electrons
Subtracts the proton number from the nucleon number, 24 - 12, to give 12 neutrons

items.prompt: Magnesium has proton number 12 and nucleon number 24. Explain how to work out its numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons, and state each number.

points.text: Gives period 3 because the arrangement shows three electron shells
Gives group 5 because there are 5 electrons in the outer shell

items.prompt: An element has electron arrangement 2,8,5. State its period and its group.

points.text: States the membrane lets some substances cross while keeping others out
Supports the point with an example such as food crossing in or waste crossing out while a harmful particle is refused

items.prompt: Explain, in terms of what crosses it, why the cell membrane is described as selectively permeable rather than a solid wall.

points.text: Names the nucleus as the structure controlling the cell
Names the membrane as selectively permeable, choosing what crosses rather than sealing the cell

items.prompt: Describe the job of the nucleus and of the cell membrane in an animal cell.

levels.descriptor: Explanations chain particle counts and shell arrangements to the group and period in order, with each step justified by a named particle or structure.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Explanations are broadly sound but one link between the counts or shells and the answer is asserted rather than justified.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Answers list particles or cell structures without connecting them into an explanation.
levels.label: Beginning
